comment: Honestly the price bump doesn't matter to me, I already cancelled the family plan over the home screen being packed with podcasts I never play. Show me the music and I'll come back, until then it's a no from me.
Paying more when ads still play in my podcasts is just insulting. The only reason I pay is ad-free music, and if they keep shoving podcasts down my throat I'll look at YouTube Premium again.

Spotify raises the price by a dollar and the artists still get a fraction of a cent per stream. Where is that extra money going, because it's not going to the people making the music. This is exactly the greed I expected.
Price going up is fine if it comes with the features they removed. Right now I'm paying more for a version that has less than before, and they still haven't explained why the old stuff vanished.
A dollar more is still cheap for what I get. No ads, offline downloads, casting, it's still more value than my other subscriptions put together. I just wish the app stopped changing every few weeks.
Can't afford the extra dollar some months as it is. I'll probably drop back to free and just deal with the shuffle again.
Not paying for it either way, I'm on the free tier and I'm staying there. If the ads get worse I might come back, but a dollar more won't change my choice.
They're raising the price on a plan that still has no lossless. Tidal has hi-fi at the same price and I'm already there, so this just makes the case for leaving Spotify stronger.
Spotify charges more and still has lossy audio and a messy library. Apple Music has lossless and Spatial Audio in the same plan, so I'm moving over to Apple Music.

Cool, now it costs more and the renewal popup still shows up every time I open the app even though I cancelled. Clearing cache didn't help and reinstalling didn't either, so I just kind of tune it out now.
Price doesn't affect me much since I keep auto-updates off and run an older version. I'll stay as long as they don't force the new layout on me, which is the real threat here.
A dollar more for Premium is still a good bang for the buck given the catalog. I'd be more worried about the free tier getting worse than about this.

The student price going from $4.99 to $5.99 really stings, especially since the Hulu bundle is what made it worth it for me. If it goes up much more I'm going back to Apple Music, they have the student plan with Apple TV.

Price going up for features I keep seeing removed, like manual album radio, and the radio still repeats songs I already know. I'll keep using stats.fm to fill the gaps but it's getting harder to justify.
Another price bump on an app that still breaks after every update. Reinstalling and running the old version are the only things that work for me, so I'm not sure what I'm paying more for.
Raising the price while the home screen is still TikTok junk is a joke. If they keep the new home layout I'm cancelling my duo plan and moving to Tidal, I'm not paying more to stare at cards.
More money for the same app that I hate. If the new music tab layout stays I'm switching to Apple Music, there's no way I'm paying extra for this.
A dollar more for the full history of recorded music is still an incredible deal. If anything it should go up more, and I'd rather that money reach artists than sit on the table.

Paying more for Premium when I still can't see liked songs inside a playlist or stop enhance from adding junk? Not a chance. If they keep removing playlist features I'll end my subscription like I already did once.
Price is fine by me, the library and Discover Weekly still beat anything else I've tried. The repetitive radio is annoying but I'd rather fix that than move to Apple Music.
The price keeps going up while the UI keeps getting worse and the recommendations keep going stale. If the next redesign is as bad as the last one, I'm moving to YouTube Music and not looking back.
A dollar more on the family plan still works out to a couple dollars per person, which is fine for an ad-free account for each of us. We'll stay on it.
Spotify pays artists less than Tidal and still doesn't have lossless, and now the price goes up. I've been using Tidal for the audio anyway, so this just makes switching more obvious for me.
More money for shuffle that still plays the same 20 songs from my 200-song playlist. Smart shuffle keeps stuffing recommendations into my playlists, and I'm already looking at Apple Music.
I'm not paying more for an app that keeps taking features away, like the liked marks on album tracks. If they don't bring those back I'll unsubscribe again, same as before.

Price up and I still can't see liked tracks in a playlist, and the video clips keep auto-playing while I browse. I'd pay an add-on for the heart button back, but I'm not paying more for this, I might switch back to Apple Music.
